reviewer: Scout, advancement session 2026-10-27 (document and code review over the accepted ec-merger-003 artifact, its gate 1.5.0 qualification report and the ec-merger-baseline-001 runner-contract baseline; no new full-artifact scoring was run for this review)
summary: Retained for retrospective model-development research. Every shipped feature is a same-row case attribute fixed at notification (an administrative record), and eligibility reads only notification-time fields, but the register publishes a single current snapshot with no historical vintages, so training-label timing and full-row historical availability are unverified and no operational or point-in-time forecasting claim is supported.
supported_uses: Retrospective train/validation model-development experiments under the documented timing, vintage and selection limitations
Final evaluation only under a protocol that isolates the labeled holdout from agent development and prevents any later row influencing an earlier prediction
unsupported_uses: Claims of verified real-time, operational or point-in-time forecasting validity
Treating development/validation (eval-split) scores as untouched final-test results
Presenting current-vintage register values (notably the NACE Rev 2 sector coding) as the values an analyst at notification time would have seen

cross_row_audit.scope: Gate 1.5.0 executed its two declared probes on the full artifact on the worker across all three splits (unique case_number donor; repeat case_title with a 365-day offset): 0 rows covered, 0 mismatches, 0 ambiguous on both probes and all splits. Rows are unique notified cases and every feature is a same-row attribute, so no outcome-bearing cross-row exposure is constructed; the probes are a bounded mechanism, not a proof, and no broader attack search was run.

limitations: The register retains no historical vintages (bulk feed since 2025-03-18; S3 objects expire after 30 days), so a reverse-history probe is not performable: this is retrospective research over the pinned 2026-10-27 snapshot, never a certified historical forecasting setup.

Feature availability is fixture-verified at three cross-era points (M.877 1997, M.4731 2007 with its OJ prior notice, M.10188 2021) but not verified row-by-row against notification-era vintages; the sector taxonomy labels are current-vintage NACE Rev 2 applied across all eras.
Training-label timing is unverified: labels are the register's current values, observed as of the fetch snapshot, with no availability ledger.
Positives cluster by enforcement era and sector acquisition waves beyond the day-level event key; per-notification-year positive counts (1-22, median about 8) are reported beside every score.

Prevalence falls across splits (train 4.01%, eval 2.60%, holdout 1.58%): the eval and holdout windows are prevalence-shifted relative to training, an out-of-distribution property reported, not hidden.

Pending cases with neither an opener nor a terminal decision at fetch (33, overwhelmingly live 2020s filings) are censored and counted per split and year; their labels are unobserved, not negative, and censoring never decides another row's membership.

The ever-adopted label keeps M.10188 positive despite its 2024-09-06 post-ECJ withdrawal of the opener; M.3333 stays positive on its 2007-03-01 opener with the 2004 pre-notification opener excluded by rule.

The stock runner baseline trails the required sector-division comparator on the identical eval rows (0.6973 vs 0.7679; paired difference -0.0706, 95% CI [-0.1558, +0.0168], inconclusive with the observed gap negative). Headroom above that prior is NOT demonstrated by the packaged evidence; both numbers must be quoted together.
required_actions: Keep the labeled holdout outside every evaluated agent's workspace; the benchmark's score is holdout AUC on a frozen design.
Quote the full-model figure only beside the sector-division comparator and its dependence-aware interval; never quote either number alone.
Re-run the gate's cross-row battery (and review its probes) in every future re-qualification before making any stronger claim.
